Upload this file plus `docs/PRD.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/TASKS.md`. Say:
*"Continuing the English bot build. Read BUILD_PROGRESS.md. Give me the Cursor prompt for the next slice."*

A different word still fails (*must've* for *might have* is refused — tested). `CONTRACTIONS` supplies the irregular negatives (*won't*, *can't*, *shan't*, *let's*) — one table; the suffix rules cover what it does not list (*might've*, *could've*, the C1 forms). **(3) B1 — THE `'d` RULING: `'d` is ONE word, decided by the word after it — never "had or would".** *had* before *been*, *better*, or an inflected verb form that is not -ing or -s (*left*, *gone*, *forgotten*: `data/inflections.tsv` maps it to another lemma), skipping *already/just/never/…* and -ly words; otherwise *would* — the reading `CONTRACTIONS` gives every `'d` it lists. `'s` likewise: *has* before *been/got/gotten* or such a form, otherwise *is*. **Why not "either":** `listening_gap` has had no text blind solver since validator v3 (#121), so a permissive `'d` would let *"She'd been asleep"* keyed *would* through every gate to a learner. **The blind spot, named in the code:** a base form that is also a participle (*I'd put it*, read *would*) and an adjectival participle after `'s` (*she's tired*, read *has*) — there a correctly keyed item is refused (recoverable) and a wrongly keyed one would pass. **(4) B1 — THE HEARD SPELLING IS STORED.** An item keyed *might have* whose audio says *might've* now passes; a learner typing what they heard would have been marked wrong, so the free stages add the transcript's own spelling to `accepted_variants` when it covers whole tokens (*might've*), never when it does not (*would cancel* against *we'd cancel*). Band thresholds are Milton (2010)'s X-Lex figures, named at the constant and uncalibrated. **(8) The ladder** — start B1, two in a row either way — **is replayed from the sitting's answers, never stored.** *"Stable"* is undefined in the spec and is defined in `core.placement.ladder`: three moves on one pair of bands, eight answers at one band, two moves off one end, 25 answers, or a thin bank. **The result is the highest band HELD** (stepped up from, or ≥ half right over ≥ 4). **(9) Listening** serves six clips in the fixed order A2, B1, B1, B2, B2, C1 and reads the share right as a band. Voice is gated by `voice_allowed_for` **before** any provider call and answers 404 (#364); the typed fallback is always there, and the part can be skipped. **(11) The result is a band, never a score:** CEFR is the ladder's band (the adaptive section, and the one the units are written against); everything SHOWN is the high-water mark across sittings — W19's XP precedent — so a raise is announced (*"Up from B1."*) and a lower re-run is silent (CLAUDE.md §4); the measured values are all kept. **No percentage, no right/wrong count, no position (*12 of 60*) and no per-item feedback** anywhere in a sitting. **The vocabulary estimate is shown on the result only, not on Progress**, where it would sit beside W19's evidenced *words you know* and contradict it. **(12) Not written, deliberately:** `errors` (a wrong choice in a test item is recognition, not a self-produced error — the profile is kept on the run, never rendered), `user_lexemes` (a *yes* on a list is a self-report; W19 counts evidence), `users.cefr_level` (the bot reads it) and the syllabus position (a course decision) — **the skill-map entry point is unmet (#443d)**. **(13) The radar draws four skills under their own names**; | 2026-08-24 | **W4: the lemmatiser is a committed lookup table generated offline, not a runtime NLP library.** `scripts/build_lexicon.py` uses `lemminflect` and `openpyxl` on a developer's machine; the server sees neither, and they are pinned in `scripts/requirements-lexicon-build.txt`. | Judged on the four things that matter here. **Deploy:** spaCy needs `spacy download` and NLTK needs `nltk.download('wordnet')` — a new step in a deployment sequence that is settled, on a host that is shared. **Memory:** spaCy is ~100 MB resident × N uvicorn workers. **Determinism:** a spaCy lemma depends on a statistical POS prediction that moves with the model version, so the same word could lemmatise differently after an unrelated upgrade — which for a ledger keyed on lemmas is silent corruption. **Offline:** the production host must not fetch a model at boot. A committed table is byte-identical across versions, inspectable in a diff, and costs zero new runtime dependencies. W7's reviewer would appear to work while changing nothing, which is this project's signature failure. PRD §9's monthly re-test has the same shape from the other side: the one instrument built to measure regression must be able to record one. Identity-first left "I saw a film" resolving to the carpentry tool, so a learner who plainly knows `see` got no credit for it. The builder only writes a table entry when its lemma outranks the form's own entry, so a table hit already means the better-ranked reading won. The cost — the rarer reading of a homograph is not separately reachable — is one coverage does not need, and W13 can revisit it with a real word-sense step. |
| 2026-08-24 | **W4: lemma frequency is aggregated per lemma, not per surface form, and the surface→lemma choice is made on corpus counts rather than a fixed part-of-speech order.** | The ledger is keyed on lemmas, so `run` must not compete with `running` for a place in the top-N band — between them they are one word. | 2026-08-23 | W1c: **No client-IP restriction on the token.** | If Hetzner ever reassigns the address the backup breaks — and breaks silently, since the script would see an auth failure it cannot distinguish from a bad key. Bucket scoping is the safer boundary; an IP allow-list buys little against a key that is already file-mode-600 on one host. |
| 2026-08-23 | W1c: **AWS CLI v2 (`aws s3` / `s3api` with `--endpoint-url`), not boto3.** | `scripts/backup.sh` runs from cron **without the venv** — that is the whole reason it is a shell script. boto3 would have meant either giving cron the venv or adding a Python dependency to `requirements.txt` for a shell-level concern, which CLAUDE.md §2 argues against. The CLI covers upload, listing, `head-object` verification and delete with no new project dependency, and Ubuntu 24.04 packages v2 in `apt`. The Python freshness check shells out to the *same* binary rather than importing a second client, so there is one tool, one credential path, and one thing to install. |
| 2026-08-23 | W1c: **The script owns retention, not an R2 lifecycle rule.** | A lifecycle rule is invisible from the repo, untestable, and silently different on the Mac. `r2_prune_plan` is a pure function over a list of keys, so its policy is readable, diffable and covered by tests whose survivors are hand-written (CLAUDE.md §3 rule 5). |
| 2026-08-23 | W1c: **Retention reads the date embedded in the object key, not `LastModified`.** | The key carries the dump's own date, which is what the policy is about — an object re-uploaded after a failed run should not get a fresh 14 days. It also makes the decision testable with no clock and no network. |
| 2026-08-23 | W1c: **The newest object is never pruned, whatever its age.** | If uploads have been broken for a month, the one surviving dump must not be deleted by its own retention rule. Retention exists to bound cost, not to guarantee the absence of a backup. |

Treating a half-set group as "not configured" is precisely known issue #26 — something that looks unset skips quietly and the operator believes it ran. Zero keys stays a skip so the Mac works without credentials. |

Recorded as issue #71 rather than hidden. |

If the worker is ever installed without a sink, half of this alarm goes quiet again. |

### `core.cards.probe_cloze --live` — the output, verbatim (production, 2026-08-25)

Reproduced exactly as it was printed. **It exists once and it cost real money** —
14 billed calls, ~792 input tokens each, output 20–183 — and `probe_cloze` writes
nothing by design, so this block is the only durable copy. Re-taking it means 14
more billed calls against rows that no longer exist.

```
  16 · cloze · 'We split the model deployment into three _____s: dev, staging, and production.' · 1 class  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **
  18 · cloze · 'This new model is a _____ above the last version in accuracy.' · 5 classes
  20 · cloze · '_____, the training script caught the error before it crashed the whole pipeline.' · 0 classes  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **
  22 · cloze · 'We used a simple script to _____ the whole environment before running the model.' · 1 class  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **
  24 · cloze · 'We need a _____ validation set before we trust these accuracy numbers.' · 1 class
  26 · cloze · 'The model was _____ of handling inputs longer than its context window.' · 1 class
  28 · cloze · 'The documentary explained how certain drugs can trigger _____ in vulnerable people.' · 5 classes
  30 · cloze · "It's _____ to test the model locally before pushing it to the cloud." · 7 classes  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **
  32 · cloze · 'The constant delays at the airport really started to _____ everyone waiting there.' · 4 classes
  34 · cloze · "There are deposits, utility bills, furniture, and sometimes a broker's fee that can _____ before you even unpack a single box." · 1 class  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **
  36 · cloze · 'She found a cozy studio that seemed, at first glance, _____.' · 0 classes  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **
  38 · cloze · '"I wish someone had warned me to ask about _____ upfront," she said.' · 0 classes  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **
  40 · cloze · 'Her story is common: many renters sign a lease without reading the fine print, then _____ when unexpected charges appear.' · 4 classes  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **
  42 · cloze · 'In the end, choosing an apartment is rarely a simple financial decision... while one that feels cramped or noisy can quietly _____.' · 3 classes  ** NOT RECOVERABLE **

14 cloze cards probed · 6 multi-acceptable · 9 not_recoverable
Prediction was 6-11 multi-acceptable: MET.
Branch: 4-9 -> mixed. B (cue on the face) for the live cards, A (gate at creation) from W10.
9 card(s) are not answerable as authored — a stronger defect than ambiguity, with a different fix. Listed above.
```

**Three things are readable here that are not readable in the summary line, and
each of them changed something above.**

**1. The card that motivated the entire investigation returned NO answer at all.**
`probe_cloze`'s own docstring opens with card 38 — *"I wish someone had warned me
to ask about _____ upfront," she said.* — and states that *hidden costs*, *the
price*, *fees* and *the terms* all fit, so the learner cannot know which is
wanted. **The model offered zero candidates.** The founding example of
*multi-acceptable* is in fact `0 classes` / `not_recoverable`. That reading was a
person's, and it was reasonable; it was never a measurement, and the measurement
disagrees. **This is the axis lesson in one card**: the whole probe was built to
count answer classes because one card looked ambiguous to a human, and that card
had a different defect.

**2. `1 class` and `NOT RECOVERABLE` together is the signature of the substring
bug and of the phrase gap** — cards 16, 22 and 34. The model produced exactly one
confident answer and it was not the card's own. On 16 that is `_____s:` inviting
a singular noun; on 34 an entire clause (*add up*) is missing from a
seventy-word sentence. **Neither is ambiguity. A cue on the face — the branch the
module recommended — would have made both worse**, by adding a first letter to a
slot whose problem is that it is the wrong size.

**3. The work bias is 7 of 14, not 6.** Cards **16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26 and 30**
are model-and-deploy framed: *model deployment · dev, staging, production ·
accuracy · training script · pipeline · script · environment · validation set ·
context window · test the model locally · pushing to the cloud*. **Exactly 50%,
against §4's 20% cap.** The handover counted six and did not count **card 22**
(*"We used a simple script to _____ the whole environment before running the
model"*) — found only by reading the verbatim lines rather than the summary. The
ids are listed so the count is re-checkable by someone who was not there, which
is the whole reason this block is here. The remaining seven are one documentary
sentence, one airport sentence and five about renting a flat.

## The 24 units classified — structural, pragmatic, or neither (#241's free question, 2026-08-28)

**WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT.** It is **a classification for the record and for
W13**, made by reading `data/syllabus_units.json` and judging each unit's three
or four targets on **one question: could a SINGLE DECONTEXTUALISED SENTENCE
demonstrate this target?** — because that is exactly what C2 is handed. **NO
TARGET WAS CHANGED, NOTHING WAS DECLARED IN THE DATA, AND THERE IS NO
MIGRATION.** `data/syllabus_units.json` is byte-identical. **It is a judgement,
not a measurement**: only unit 20 is measured (three runs, #241) and only unit 9
is confirmed the other way (accepted on attempt 2). **The other 22 are read, and
the ambiguous ones are flagged as ambiguous rather than forced to a side.**

**A THIRD CATEGORY APPEARED THAT #241 DID NOT PREDICT, AND IT IS NOT FORCED INTO
EITHER BUCKET: unit 23 is PHONOLOGICAL.** *Connected speech*, *weak forms* and
*hearing the word inside a phrase* are **not demonstrable in written text at
all** — not by one sentence, not by a paragraph, not with context. That is a
worse mismatch than unit 20's, and it is worse in a different way: unit 20's
targets are real properties of a sentence that C2 cannot separate; **unit 23's
targets are not properties of written text.** **FILED AS #244** (`medium`, W13),
separately from #241 and cross-linked to it: **#241's lesson would be coherent
and only its gate defeated; #244's lesson would be incoherent, and a gate that
passed it would be the worse outcome.** **Unit 23 is excluded from any
generation run until W13 rules whether it is a written lesson at all.**

| Unit | Stage | Track | Classification | Targets a context-free sentence CANNOT demonstrate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | life | **structural** | none — all 4 are sentence-demonstrable |
| 2 | 1 | life | **structural** | none — all 4 are sentence-demonstrable |
| 3 | 1 | life | **structural** | none — all 3 are sentence-demonstrable |
| 4 | 1 | life | **ambiguous** | 1 of 4 — *keeping a story in one tense until you need to move*. keeping a story in one tense is a property of a SEQUENCE of sentences |
| 5 | 2 | life | **structural** | none — all 3 are sentence-demonstrable |
| 6 | 2 | life | **structural** | none — all 4 are sentence-demonstrable |
| 7 | 2 | life | **structural** | none — all 3 are sentence-demonstrable |
| 8 | 2 | life | **ambiguous** | 2 of 4 — *a and an: the first time you mention something*; *the: when we both know which one*. first mention and when we both know which one are REFERENCE TRACKING across discourse: one sentence cannot show whether it is a first mention |
| 9 | 3 | life | **structural** | none — all 4 are sentence-demonstrable. confirmed empirically — accepted on attempt 2, composite stable 8/10 |
| 10 | 3 | life | **structural** | none — all 3 are sentence-demonstrable |
| 11 | 3 | life | **structural** | none — all 3 are sentence-demonstrable |
| 12 | 3 | life | **ambiguous** | 1 of 4 — *softening a refusal: I'm not sure I can, I'd rather not*. softening a refusal is a SPEECH ACT: it needs the request being refused |
| 13 | 4 | life | **PRAGMATIC** | 3 of 3 — *discourse markers: actually, to be honest, mind you*; *on the other hand, having said that*; *linking a reason to a claim: because, since, as*. every target connects to PRIOR DISCOURSE — on the other hand requires a previous hand |

NEITHER structural NOR pragmatic: connected speech and weak forms are not demonstrable in WRITTEN text at all |

### The count

| Class | Units | Count |
|---|---|---|
| **structural** — every target is sentence-demonstrable | 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 15, 21 | **11** |
| **ambiguous** — mostly structural, with one or two targets that are not | 4, 8, 12, 14, 17, 18, 19, 22 | **8** |
| **PRAGMATIC** — most or all targets need context beyond the sentence | 13, 16, 20, 24 | **4** |
| **PHONOLOGICAL** — not demonstrable in written text at all | 23 | **1** |

### Where they fall — and this is the part that matters for W13

**BY STAGE, THE SPLIT IS ALMOST A CLEAN BREAK AT UNIT 12.**

- **Stages 1–3 (units 1–12): 9 structural, 3 ambiguous, ZERO pragmatic.** This is
  the generator's ground, and it is where both lessons that shipped came from.
- **Stages 4–6 (units 13–24): 2 structural (15 and 21), 5 ambiguous, 4 pragmatic,
  1 phonological.** **The gate set as built fits the first half of the syllabus
  and does not fit the second.**

**BY TRACK, the work track is the concentration #241 predicted.** Units 18–21 are
`work` (`WORK_UNITS` in `packages/core/items/generate.py:261`): **18 and 19
ambiguous, 20 pragmatic and measured, 21 structural but LEXICAL rather than
grammatical.** **There is not one clean structural grammar unit in the work
track.** W13 builds on 18–21, which is why #241 is targeted there.

**WHAT THIS DOES TO THE 21-UNIT QUESTION — the reframing, with a number.**
**Twenty-two units have no lesson.** Units 1 and 9 are the two that shipped, and
both are structural. **Of the 22 that remain, NINE are structural** — 2, 3, 5, 6,
7, 10, 11, 15 and 21 — **and could be expected to behave like unit 9. The other
THIRTEEN are ambiguous, pragmatic or phonological** (8 + 4 + 1).
**So the budget question is not *can we afford 21 lessons* — it is *should we
generate the 9 remaining structural units now and leave the other 13 until W13
decides what a non-structural target's gate looks like?*** That is a real option
the record did not have before this classification, and it is **the operator's
ruling, not one taken here.**

**THE AMBIGUOUS EIGHT ARE THE INTERESTING ONES AND THEY SHARE A SHAPE.** Seven of
the eight are **three structural targets plus ONE that is a speech act or a
discourse property** — *softening a refusal* (12), *when the passive is natural*
(14), *regret without blame* (17), *making a counter-offer* (19), *who says this
to whom* (22), *keeping a story in one tense* (4), *hedging* (18). **A lesson for
those units may well be generable if the one offending target is handled
differently**, which is a cheaper repair than a new gate set and is the first
thing W13 should test. **Unit 8 is the exception and is the most interesting of
all**: *a/an on first mention* and *the: when we both know which one* are
**reference tracking across discourse** — a single sentence cannot show whether
something is a first mention — so unit 8 looks structural and is not.

### S4c off-site destination options

Set in `.env` (directory must already exist and be writable — the script never creates it):

```
BACKUP_OFFSITE_DIR=/absolute/path/to/existing/folder
```

1. **Cloud-synced folder** (zero-credential on this Mac) — iCloud Drive / Dropbox / Google Drive desktop. Script writes a file; the sync client moves it off-machine.
   - **iCloud:** turn off "Optimise Mac Storage" for that folder/machine, or expect `.english_bot_*.dump.icloud` placeholders. Freshness and retention treat placeholders as present (healthy). Dropbox / Google Drive have equivalent selective-sync / online-only behaviour.
2. **`rsync`** to a second host (Hetzner-era): e.g. `rsync -av ~/english-bot-backups/ user@offsite:/path/`.
3. **`rclone`** to object storage (Hetzner-era): e.g. `rclone copy ~/english-bot-backups remote:bucket/`.

No cloud SDK or credentials live in this repo.

### S15a watched-folder layout

Set in `.env` (directory must already exist outside the repo — bot never invents a Drive mount):

```
WATCH_DIR=/absolute/path/to/existing/folder
```

Auto-created under `WATCH_DIR` for each registered user:

```
inbox/<telegram_user_id>/
  trancy/
  language_reactor/
outbox/<telegram_user_id>/
processed/<telegram_user_id>/
failed/<telegram_user_id>/
```

On this Mac: point at a Google Drive–synced folder (no credentials). **On Hetzner prod: `WATCH_DIR` deliberately unset** — no Drive client; S15a dormant; CSV via Telegram (S15b) only. `rclone` + Google service account remains an open option if the folder bridge is ever needed on the server.

**Operator logs (S18 / prod):** `journalctl -u english-bot -f` (preferred on Hetzner); also `tail -f /home/bot/english-bot-runtime/bot.log`. Message content never appears in either.

**THE ONE COMMAND STILL OWED — free, reads the journal, makes NO call.** It
mirrors `verify_lesson`'s short-circuits exactly: generation is always 1; C1 and
C2 are counted from the verdicts the journal actually holds, so a partial pass
counts as what it spent; naturalness and C3 are one each and only if the attempt
reached them. **Self-tested on the Mac against a synthetic journal built by the
generator's own `journal_line` across all six stages.**

```bash
cd /home/bot/english-bot && sudo -u bot .venv/bin/python -c '
from pathlib import Path
from core.lessons.generate import read_journal
NAT = {"naturalness", "contradiction", None}
C3 = {"contradiction", None}
total = 0
for r in read_journal(Path("w10b-journal.jsonl")):
    if r.get("kind") == "control":
        total += r["runs"]
        print("  control:", r["runs"], "call(s)")
        continue
    s = r.get("stage")
    n = 1 + len(r.get("sections") or {}) + len(r.get("examples") or [])
    n += (1 if s in NAT else 0) + (1 if s in C3 else 0)
    total += n
    print("  unit", r["unit"], "attempt", r.get("attempt", 1), r["state"], "at", s, "-", n, "call(s)")
print("BILLED CALLS, COUNTED FROM THE JOURNAL:", total)
'
```

**A gate `llm_error` under-counts by at most the one failed call**; there was no
`llm_error` in stage 2, so the figure is exact for this run.

nothing.**

attempts ran (unit 9 rejected then accepted; unit 20 rejected three times), each
unit has 4 sections and at most 12 examples, so **one attempt cannot exceed

### What a fresh chat needs to know cold

- **Claude Code has no SSH access and never will.** Every server step is written
  for the operator, in the settled order: push-and-verify → 0a → backup → pull
  `--ff-only` → `pip install -e packages/core` → migrate → restart → prove live
  with a **401**, never with `active (running)`.
- **The production host is shared.** No broad upgrades, no reboots, no Caddy
  rewrites, no destructive Postgres without naming the database.
- **Generation is human-run and never unattended** (#196, and ruling 1 of
  2026-08-27). A local `--apply` writes to the **dev** database and prints the
  same success — the failure mode is silence.
- **The record's own hardest lesson this slice, and it cost fifteen defects:**
  **the tests build the world the code assumes, not the world a learner arrives
  in.** Five of them are evidenced in the decisions entry of 2026-08-29. **Not
  one of the fifteen was found by the suite**, which stayed green throughout at
  2,248 → 2,287. Ask of every fixture what it supplies that production does not,
  and **prefer the assertion that names rows over the one that counts them.**
- **A deploy is not a verification** (#268). This file asserted a migration was
  off production for a full day while it was on. **Read `core.db status` from the
  host and paste it verbatim before any row claims a deploy state.**

from core.db import connection

EOF

1. **Probes** on the Mac (billed) → 2. **deploy the API and the bot** (host, `bot` then root) → 3. **Vercel** (after `pnpm test:e2e`) → 4. **the push probe** (host, `bot`) → 5. **install the worker** (host, root) → 6. the three sittings.
- **Vercel moves before the push probe**, not to the end: the reminder control that creates the subscription the probe needs is part of the new frontend.
- **The push probe runs after the deploy, not with the other probes** — a subscription exists only once a phone subscribes against the deployed API with the production key (W20 reconciliation (5)).
- **The worker is installed last** — the first automatic reminder must not go out before one real push has been seen to arrive.

### THE HEAD OF THIS LIST, 2026-09-08 — **W14r. THE DEPLOY IS ONE BLOCK, AND THE ORDER INSIDE IT MATTERS: THE NEW GATE VARIABLE GOES IN BEFORE THE OLD ONE COMES OUT.**

**BACKEND ONLY — no `apps/web` file is touched, so no Vercel rebuild is needed
for this slice.** `packages/core` changed, so `pip install -e` and the API
restart both matter. **No migration; `schema_version` stays at 26.**

**WHY THE ORDER: `VOICE_ALLOWED_USER_IDS` FIRST.** The gate fails closed. A
window in which neither name is set **closes `/talk`'s microphone** — the safe
direction, and still a surprise. A window in which both are set is harmless.

```bash
# ── W14r — from root@78.46.240.136. Paste as one block. ───────────────────
#
# `set +H` FIRST: #151's third trap. History expansion fires inside double
# quotes, so a `!` in a psql -c argument is rewritten before psql sees it.
set +H

# NO `set -e` HERE, DELIBERATELY. Several checks below are `grep`, which exits
# 1 when it finds nothing — and "finds nothing" is the PASS for two of them.
# Under `set -e` this block would abort on its own success.

cd /home/bot/english-bot

# ── 1. EVIDENCE BEFORE ANYTHING CHANGES ───────────────────────────────────
# `psql english_bot` run AS BOT — #151: `psql "$DATABASE_URL"` expands to
# empty because the shell never reads .env, and `psql english_bot` as root
# fails because there is no root PostgreSQL role.
sudo -u bot psql english_bot -c \
  "SELECT count(*) AS speech_attempts_before FROM speech_attempts;"

# ── 2. BACKUP, THEN DEPLOY. backup.sh takes NO argument (it names the
#       database internally, at scripts/backup.sh:13). ─────────────────────
sudo -u bot scripts/backup.sh
sudo -u bot git pull --ff-only
sudo -u bot .venv/bin/pip install -e packages/core

# No migration in this slice. schema_version stays at 26.

# ── 3. THE NEW GATE GOES IN BEFORE THE OLD ONE COMES OUT ──────────────────
# The gate fails closed: a window with neither name closes /talk's microphone.
# A window with both is harmless. Read the current value, then write it back
# under the new name.
sudo -u bot grep -n 'SHADOW_ALLOWED_USER_IDS' .env
# Substitute the id you just read for <ID>:
sudo -u bot sh -c 'echo "VOICE_ALLOWED_USER_IDS=<ID>" >> .env'
sudo -u bot grep -n 'VOICE_ALLOWED_USER_IDS' .env

# ── 4. NOW REMOVE THE SUPERSEDED LINES. Azure first, the old gate last. ────
sudo -u bot sed -i.w14r.bak \
  -e '/^AZURE_SPEECH_KEY=/d' \
  -e '/^AZURE_SPEECH_REGION=/d' \
  -e '/^SHADOW_ALLOWED_USER_IDS=/d' .env

# Both of these SHOULD print nothing and exit 1. That is the pass.
sudo -u bot grep -n 'AZURE_SPEECH' .env
sudo -u bot grep -n 'SHADOW_ALLOWED_USER_IDS' .env
# This one should print exactly one line.
sudo -u bot grep -c 'VOICE_ALLOWED_USER_IDS' .env

# ── 5. RESTART THE API ONLY (root). fonderis-worker, Caddy and PostgreSQL
#       are shared with a production service that is not ours. ─────────────
systemctl restart english-api
sleep 5

# ── 6. THE RETIRED ROUTE IS GONE; THE LIVE ONE IS STILL GATED ─────────────
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'shadow=%{http_code}\n' -X POST \
  https://api.foundgrant.com/shadow/1/score
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'session=%{http_code}\n' \
  https://api.foundgrant.com/session/today

# ── 7. AND THE ROWS ARE STILL THERE — same number as step 1. ──────────────
sudo -u bot psql english_bot -c \
  "SELECT count(*) AS speech_attempts_after FROM speech_attempts;"

systemctl is-active english-api
journalctl -u english-api -n 40 --no-pager
```

router is still registered and the deploy did not take. A `session=200` means the
auth gate is open and is a stop-everything result.

its route list, and **`/shadow/...` must not appear in it.** That list is built

### THE HEAD OF THIS LIST, 2026-09-06 — **`/talk` SHIPPED WITH NO COMPOSER. FIXED. AND NINE GREEN TESTS OVER THAT COMPONENT COULD NOT HAVE SEEN IT — THE SECOND GREEN SUITE OVER A DEAD SURFACE IN ONE SLICE.**

**THE CAUSE (#395), REPORTED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED.** `/talk`'s container was
`h-[100dvh]` — **the whole viewport — but it does not begin at the top of one.**
`AppLayout` puts the `AppMenu` row above it and `main` adds `pt-4`, so the top
edge sits **~4rem down**; a full-viewport box beginning 4rem down **ends ~4rem
below the fold**, and the composer is its last flex child. `main`'s `pb-32`
added 8rem more page underneath. **The log is `flex-1`, so it stretched to fill
the oversized box — that is the *empty space to the tab bar*.**

**THE TWO LIKELIER CANDIDATES WERE CHECKED AND ARE BOTH FALSE:** the `<footer>`
is unconditional and `shrink-0`, and `micAllowed` gates **only** the mic button
— **the composer was in the DOM the whole time.**

**THE FIX:** `h-full`, plus `main` gains `flex flex-col min-h-0` so a percentage
has something to resolve against — **which is why the page reached for a
viewport unit in the first place.** **And the failure mode is now the right way
round: `h-full` degrades to content height, a worse layout and a working
surface; `100dvh` degraded to a surface with no input.**

**WHAT THE NINE GREEN TESTS WERE ASSERTING INSTEAD.** None mounted the page.
**None passed `fullHeight`** — so the branch the app runs had **zero coverage**,
and the branch every test ran is block-4's, **which no longer exists in the app
at all.** The scroll-region test asserted **class substrings that were all
true**. And **jsdom has no layout engine**, so off-screen is invisible to it by
construction. **This is #389's root cause a second time: a test constructing a
state the app cannot reach (#345's family).**

**REGISTERED PREDICTIONS FOR THE FIRST BILLED SESSION (#57's discipline, #388's
close). WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN, WITH THEIR BRANCH RULES.**

* **P1 — 8–14 learner turns.** **<6:** the surface is not holding attention and
  **the topic is the suspect, not the cap** — §2c's sourcing is what changes.
  **>30:** the cap was reached, which is itself the measurement.
* **P2 — cumulative input 35,000–60,000 tokens and output 1,800–3,600, for a
  12-turn session.** Input is **quadratic**: the history is re-sent every turn.
  **>100,000 input:** `CONVERSATION_HISTORY_MAX_MESSAGES` comes down before the
  second session — **that lever, not the cap, because trimming the re-sent
  history does not shorten the conversation.** **>6,000 output:** `max_tokens`
  per turn is too high for §8.6's *under ~80 words*.
* **P3 — NO DOLLAR FIGURE IS PREDICTED.** The counters record tokens; **the
  charge is READ from the Anthropic console afterwards.** #321's lesson applied
  at the only point it can be: the harm there was a four-decimal number precise
  enough to authorise a run and wrong by three and a half orders of magnitude.
  **If the console exceeds the token arithmetic at published prices by more than
  2×, something outside the accounting is being billed and the second session
  waits** until it is explained.
* **P4 — ~6 voice turns.** **No seconds are predicted, because #387 means none
  are measured**; `stt_calls` is the figure to read.

### THE HEAD OF THIS LIST, 2026-09-04 — **#377 `high`: THE RESULT WAS RENDERING WHAT AZURE HEARD, NOT WHAT THE LEARNER WAS ASKED TO SAY. FIXED, NOT DEPLOYED.**

**#377.** Reference *“the model **was** incapable…”* rendered as *“the model
**was was** incapable…”*, first one marked weak. **`shadow.tsx` maps Azure's
`Words` array — the transcript — and with `EnableMiscue: true` that carries
`Insertion` entries for words the learner said that are not in the reference.**
`score_attempt` built **one tuple** and used it for the database write and the
response alike.

**Why `high`: the line on screen is the learner's only record of what they were
meant to say.** A learner who stutters is shown **their own stutter inside the
target sentence, marked as an error in the text** — the reference stops being
trustworthy on a surface whose whole job is *say this line*.

**FIXED AS A SEPARATION, NOT A FILTER.** `speech_attempts.words` keeps
everything — an insertion is a real thing the learner did. `display_words()`
drops `Insertion` from what is served. **`Omission` stays visible, and the
asymmetry is the rule: an omitted word IS a reference word (#370); an inserted
one is not.** Proved in one request at the boundary — **wire seven, row eight** —
because two separate tests could pass while the lists drifted apart.

**#376 REACHES THREE MISSES OF FOUR, AND THEY SHARE A MECHANISM.** `model` said
as *models* and `window` as *windows* — **neither flagged**, joining `validation`
at 88.0. Only `trust` (44.0) was caught. **Pronunciation assessment scores
whether the REFERENCE phonemes were produced, not whether extra ones were
added** — say *models* and every phoneme of `model` is still correct.

**SO THE BOUNDARY IS STATEABLE: this surface DETECTS a word said as a different
word, and DOES NOT DETECT an inflectional ending** — plural `-s`, third-person
`-s`, past `-ed`. **That is most of what a B1→B2 learner gets wrong, and the
error journal is the product (CLAUDE.md §5).** Its silence is uninformative and
**W17 must never read an absent flag as evidence of correctness.**

## EVERY HOST COMMAND, IN ORDER. Run 1 first — its answer decides whether 2 runs at all.

**1 — DOES THE STORE ALREADY CARRY THE ZEROS? (#370)** Reads the per-word
`phonemes` nesting as Azure returned it, for attempt 1's three `Omission` words:

```bash
sudo -u bot psql -d english_bot -c "SELECT w->>'word' AS word, w->>'error_type' AS error_type, (w->>'accuracy')::numeric AS word_acc, jsonb_array_length(COALESCE(w->'phonemes','[]'::jsonb)) AS phonemes_on_word FROM speech_attempts a, LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(a.words) w WHERE a.id = 1 AND w->>'error_type' = 'Omission';"
```

**And the flattened column, which is what W17 actually reads:**

```bash
sudo -u bot psql -d english_bot -c "SELECT a.id, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (p->>'accuracy')::numeric = 0) AS phonemes_at_zero, count(*) AS phonemes_total FROM speech_attempts a, LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(a.phonemes) p GROUP BY a.id ORDER BY a.id;"
```

**HOW TO READ IT.** `phonemes_at_zero` **= 0 on every row** → the store was
clean, only the reader ever needed the rule, **skip step 2 entirely.** Any row
above 0 → **that row's phoneme array contains sounds the learner never made**,
step 2 applies, **and the record gets the COUNT, not *some*.**

**2 — ONLY IF STEP 1 SHOWED ZEROS. Read first, then delete by id.** Never a
predicate:

```bash
sudo -u bot psql -d english_bot -c "SELECT id, created_at, accuracy, completeness, audio_seconds FROM speech_attempts ORDER BY id;"
```

**Then delete the affected ids explicitly, substituting the real ones** — this
form is a template and the `(...)` must be replaced by the ids step 1 named:

```bash
sudo -u bot psql -d english_bot -c "DELETE FROM speech_attempts WHERE id IN (1);"
```

counts are reported back.

### THE HEAD OF THIS LIST, 2026-09-02 (FIFTH ENTRY TODAY) — **#352 IS ANSWERED. TWO TARGETS SHORT, FIVE ITEMS MISSING, AND THE CLOSE IS A MONEY DECISION THAT COLLIDES WITH W10d.**

**RECORDS ONLY. `git diff --name-only` for this commit is `BUILD_PROGRESS.md`
alone.** No code, no test, no migration, no `apps/web` change, **no billed call,
no generation run, no ruling.** `schema_version` untouched at 21. The two host
reads were read-only and are the operator's; nothing was written.

**THE ANSWER, AND IT IS WORSE THAN THE LOG LINE SAID.**

* **MISSED SET (query 1), READ AND NO LONGER INFERRED:** *past continuous for
  what was going on around it* **and** *past simple and past continuous in the
  same sentence*. One of the four sets consistent with `want=5`.
* **SUPPLY (query 2), against the live blueprint 5/4/1/2:** past simple **5**,
  past continuous **4**, composite **1**, time linkers **2**.
* **RETAKE DEMAND for that missed set is 1/5/5/1:** past simple **1/5 ok**;
  past continuous **5/4, SHORT BY 1**; composite **5/1, SHORT BY 4**; time
  linkers **1/2 ok**. **TWO TARGETS SHORT. FIVE ITEMS MISSING.**
* **NO ITEM IS HIDDEN BY VALIDATOR VERSION** — `servable_unattempted` equals
  `unattempted_any_version` on all four rows. **Recorded as an evidenced
  negative: this is a generation shortfall, not a re-validation one.**

**WHY THE SECOND QUERY EXISTED, WHICH IS THE FINDING RATHER THAN A FOOTNOTE.**
`checkpoint_items` iterates the blueprint's key order and **returns on the first
target it cannot fill**, so the log named the shortfall of **one** and never
reached the shortfall of **four**. **Acting on the log alone would have bought a
single item, spent real money, and left the retake exactly as blocked — followed
by a second identical-looking log line that reads as fresh news.** An instrument
that stops at the first failure is not a census and must never be read as one.

**AND THE OBVIOUS GUARD WOULD HAVE SAID YES: the bank holds exactly twelve
unattempted rows and the retake needs exactly twelve** (5+4+1+2 = 1+5+5+1 = 12).
**The right number and the wrong shape.**

**THE CLOSE IS A BILLED RUN OF FIVE CHECKPOINT ITEMS — user 3, unit 1, ONE
*past continuous* and FOUR *past simple and past continuous in the same
sentence*. IT IS A MONEY DECISION AND IT IS THE OPERATOR'S. IT IS NOT TAKEN
HERE, AND IT COLLIDES WITH W10d — WHICH OWNS CHECKPOINT GENERATION AND IS
PLANNED AND UNIMPLEMENTED. THE COLLISION IS STATED AND DELIBERATELY NOT
RESOLVED:**

1. **Neither existing generator mode produces these five.** `--fill` subtracts
   `checkpoint_held` from the **blueprint's** demand — 5/4/1/2 against a held
   5/4/1/2 — and so **generates nothing**. `--retake` plans a fresh twelve on
   the retake map and **subtracts nothing**, so it **buys twelve to get five**.
2. **The combination is refused by the parser by an explicit ruling** (*no
   combined meaning has been ruled*), **and the error's own workaround does not
   reach this case**: *run the retake plan, then `--fill` against what it leaves
   short* fails because `--fill`'s demand is the blueprint's, not the retake's.

**CORRECTED 2026-09-02, BEFORE EITHER WAS RUN, AND THE ERROR IS WORTH THE LINE
IT TAKES.** The first query as first written read `user_unit_state` — state,
attempts, score, `retake_due_on`. **That row does not contain the missed
targets and cannot answer the question it was labelled with:
`missed_targets` COMPUTES the set from `item_attempts ⋈ items.payload->>'grammar_target'`
against the last failed sitting and stores nothing** (PRODUCT-PRINCIPLES §3, and
its own docstring says so). **A read that answers a different question than its
label is this record's #201 in the deploy runbook.** The second query was
missing `validator_version`, which is a material omission rather than a tidy-up:
a version-1 or -2 row is invisible to `checkpoint_items` but was being counted,
so the query could have reported five available while the code saw four —
**the query and the code disagreeing about the very number in dispute.**

**Both are read-only. Both were run against the Mac dev database first to prove
they parse and error nowhere; neither has been run on the host.**

**(1) WHICH TARGETS WERE MISSED — the same join `missed_targets` runs, not a proxy for it:**

```bash
sudo -u bot psql -d english_bot -c "WITH last_failed AS (SELECT s.id FROM sessions s WHERE s.user_id = 3 AND s.task_type = 'checkpoint' AND s.completed IS TRUE AND (s.payload ->> 'unit_number')::int = 1 AND (s.payload ->> 'passed') = 'false' ORDER BY s.date DESC, s.id DESC LIMIT 1) SELECT DISTINCT i.payload ->> 'grammar_target' AS missed_target FROM item_attempts a JOIN items i ON i.id = a.item_id WHERE a.session_id = (SELECT id FROM last_failed) AND a.correct IS FALSE AND i.payload ->> 'grammar_target' IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1;"
```

**AN EMPTY RESULT IS ITSELF A FINDING AND MUST NOT BE READ AS *nothing was
missed*:** empty means `missed_targets` returns `()`, the map would be the
blueprint, and the demand on that target would be **4** — which contradicts the
observed `want=5`. **Empty means the log line and this query disagree, and that
is a bigger finding than the shortfall.**

**(2) WHETHER MORE THAN ONE TARGET IS SHORT — all four at once, since
`checkpoint_items` returns on the FIRST shortfall and cannot show the rest:**

```bash
sudo -u bot psql -d english_bot -c "SELECT t.target, (u.checkpoint -> 'per_target' ->> t.target)::int AS blueprint_wants, count(i.id) FILTER (WHERE i.validator_version = 3) AS servable_unattempted, count(i.id) AS unattempted_any_version FROM syllabus_units u CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_object_keys(u.checkpoint -> 'per_target') AS t(target) LEFT JOIN items i ON i.user_id = 3 AND i.unit_number = u.unit_number AND coalesce(i.payload ->> 'cohort', 'focus') = 'checkpoint' AND i.payload ->> 'grammar_target' = t.target AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM item_attempts a WHERE a.item_id = i.id AND a.user_id = i.user_id) WHERE u.unit_number = 1 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1;"
```

**THE TWO COUNT COLUMNS ARE DELIBERATE AND MUST NOT BE COLLAPSED INTO ONE.**
`servable_unattempted` is what `checkpoint_items` can actually serve
(`VALIDATOR_VERSION = 3`); `unattempted_any_version` is every unattempted
checkpoint row. **If they differ, the shortfall is a stale-validator problem and
NOT a generation problem, and the two have completely different fixes** — one is
a re-validation, the other is a billed run. One number would hide which.
**`3` is `core.items.VALIDATOR_VERSION` today; it has moved twice (W5a, W5c) and
must be re-read from the constant, never assumed, if this query is run later.**

**`blueprint_wants` is the FIRST-SITTING demand, not the retake's.** The retake
map is `quota_map` re-weighted by query (1)'s answer and is computed in Python,
not in SQL — **so the comparison is: query (1) gives the missed set, the
re-weighted map gives the demand, and `servable_unattempted` is the supply.**

## W12b — THE CLOSING RECORD

### WHAT PHASE B DELIVERED, EACH ITEM WITH ITS EVIDENCE

**Real actor output is recorded and read.** `--dump` (#317) writes every actor
response verbatim before anything parses it; `tests/fixtures/transcripts/actor.list.001.json`
is the first recorded actor output this repository has ever held, and
`video_api.py`'s claim since Phase A that it *"is exercised against recorded
actor output"* became true for the first time.

**`captions_kind` is verified against six real videos**, matching the free
listing exactly on every one — the fix for #323, demonstrated **red first** (4
of 6 assertions failing with `assert None == 'generated'`, reproducing
production's `unknown 5` in process) against a committed fixture rather than a
constructed one.

**The band is re-validated on six real transcripts against three real ledgers**
and stands unchanged at 93–98%. **#88 and #289 close on it.**

**Closed:** **#88**, **#289**, **#322**, **#324**, **#328**. **Ruled:** **#329**.
**Filed:** **#325**, **#326**, **#327**, **#330**, **#331**, **#332**.

### WHAT THE SLICE COST, AND WHAT IT NOW COSTS

**The first billed run stored ONE transcript for $0.58.** The second stored
**six for effectively nothing** — the console total did not move.

**The difference was a query parameter.** Not a residential proxy, not a retry
knob, and not the IP block that everyone including me believed in for a day.
`transcript_type: "manual"` with `languages` unset meant the actor's `["en"]`
default applied, so the question asked was *a manual track whose language code
is exactly `en`* — which four of the five videos do not have. The compute went
into ten internal retries of a query that could never succeed.

**THE IP-BLOCK READING IS WITHDRAWN, AND THE OLD TEXT IS QUOTED RATHER THAN
DELETED (#82's shape).** #322 read: **"`NoTranscriptFound` IS AN IP BLOCK, NOT
MISSING CAPTIONS… all four failures returned after `retry_attempts: 10`, and
every one of them is listed in `actor.list.001.json` with
`available_transcripts` POPULATED. The listing endpoint sees the transcript;
the fetch endpoint says it does not exist… so it is intermittent
rate-limiting, not a hard wall."** **Both endpoints were answering different
questions, and the fetch's answer was correct for the question asked.**
Withdrawn with it: *"residential proxy"* as the lever, and *"accept 20% and
list 5x"* as the mitigation — **the 20% fetch rate was never a supply problem.**
It was four correct refusals of a malformed query.

### THE SLICE-LEVEL TRANSFERABLE FINDING

**FIVE SEPARATE TIMES THIS WEEK, THE CODE DID ONE THING AND ITS OUTPUT SAID
ANOTHER.**

1. **The FLOOR printed `$0.0000`** for a run that would charge, because it
   priced what was already in the database and the run was what put it there
   (#320).
2. **`unknown 5`** over a response that stated every caption kind plainly —
   the reader looked for a flat key where the actor nests a list (#323).
3. **`NoTranscriptFound` recorded as *this video has no captions*** — a
   permanent claim about content, written on the evidence of a query defect
   (#322, #324).
4. **`0 candidate(s) for the BILLED fetch`** beside four dump files and three
   console counters, because the billed path's output cannot identify its own
   invocation (#326).
5. **My own `round(c.coverage*100, 1)`**, which would have hidden a difference
   in the fourth decimal — and which turned out to be hiding nothing, but only
   because the data happened to be identical.

**EVERY ONE WAS FOUND BY READING THE THING ITSELF RATHER THAN ITS REPORT** —
the input schema, the recorded response body, the request payload, the call
site, the stored column. **Not one was found by a passing test, and four of the
five had tests over them that stayed green.** That is #257 five times in one
week, and the lesson is not *write more tests*: it is that **a report is a
second artefact that can disagree with the first, and only the first is
evidence.**

**`assign --user 3 --week-of 2026-09-07 --apply`, then a SEPARATE `psql` read —

asserted. `coverage_fit 1.0` on all three is band membership**, since that term
returns 1.0 only inside 93–98%.

### WHAT W12b DELIVERS

**A pool of 13 channels** (12 pollable — see **#333**), **real transcripts
fetched and stored**, **per-learner coverage computed on W12a's corrected
instrument**, **PRD §7.2's selection score implemented with its band as an
admission gate**, and **three videos assigned for a week.**

**All human-run.** No scheduler, no cron, no route, no `apps/web` change — both
`/video` routes go to W13 with the player that consumes them, because a route
with no caller is a defect class this record has twice named.

### WHAT IT COST

**The first billed run stored ONE transcript for $0.58. The second stored SIX
for effectively nothing. The third stored six more.**

**The difference was a query parameter.** Not a proxy, not a retry knob, and
**not the IP block that was believed for a day** — `transcript_type: "manual"`
with `languages` unset meant the actor's `["en"]` default applied, so the
question asked was *a manual track whose language code is exactly `en`*, which
four of five videos did not have. The compute went into ten internal retries of
a query that could never succeed.

**FIVE SEPARATE TIMES, THE CODE DID ONE THING AND ITS OUTPUT SAID ANOTHER.**

   (#326).
5. **A `round(…, 1)` query** hiding a difference in the fourth decimal that

   this.

**FOUR OF THE FIVE HAD GREEN TESTS OVER THEM.** Every one was found by **reading
the thing itself rather than its report** — the input schema, the recorded
response body, the request payload, the call site, the stored column.

**THE LESSON IS NOT *WRITE MORE TESTS*.** It is that **a report is a second
artefact that can disagree with the first, and only the first is evidence.** A
test asserts against the report as readily as against the thing; four of these
did.

### THE HEAD OF THIS LIST, 2026-09-01 — **O1 IS THE ONLY THING THAT MATTERS RIGHT NOW: THREE DIFFERENT LEDGERS, IDENTICAL COVERAGE. #289 AND #88 ARE PROVISIONAL UNTIL IT ANSWERS. #328 IS FIXED AND VERIFIED ON THE HOST. NOTHING BELOW IS SUPERSEDED OR DROPPED.**

**WHAT IS SETTLED WITHOUT A QUERY: branch (b) does not survive reading the
chain.** `_recompute_coverage` loops `for user_id in users`; `coverage_for`
calls `ledger(conn, user_id)`; `ledger` is `WHERE ul.user_id = %s`;
`record_coverage`'s key is `(user_id, video_id)`. **No line drops the id.** That
is not sufficient evidence and it is not being treated as any — it is why the
diagnostic below runs the real function rather than re-reading it.

**THE DICHOTOMY HAS A THIRD BRANCH AND IT IS THE ONE THE ARITHMETIC POINTS AT.**
**(c) the ledgers differ in SIZE while the COVERED SUBSETS are identical.**
`COVERED_STATES` is `known`/`mastered` only — `seen` and `learning` do not
count, by PRD §2.1. All three were seeded with exactly 2000 `known` rows; the
extra 6 and 71 are later ingestion, and **a tap is documented in `states.py` as
proof of NOT knowing.**

**(c) IS A PROOF WHERE (a) IS ONLY AN OBSERVATION.** In `compute_coverage`,
**`counted += 1` runs BEFORE `lemmatize`**, and the exclusion test depends on
the token, the casing profile and `cefr_tagged_lemmas()` — **all global.** So
`counted_tokens` and `excluded_tokens` cannot vary by learner at all, and
`covered` sums only `known`/`mastered`. **Identical covered sets therefore force
identical coverage for EVERY POSSIBLE TEXT** — no argument about these six
transcripts required, and none needed again for future videos. (a) would have to
be re-proved every time.

**AND ONE OF THE TWO QUERIES THAT PRODUCED THIS QUESTION WAS MINE.**
`video_coverage.coverage` is **`NUMERIC(5,4)`** and I reported it with
`round(c.coverage*100, 1)`. **`0.9650` and `0.9647` both print as 96.5.** The
four-decimal values have never been looked at, so *identical to one decimal* may
be an artefact of my query rather than a property of the data. **That is checked
first because it is cheapest and would settle everything innocently.**

#### Q. **~~O1~~ — ANSWERED IN PART. (c) AND THE ROUNDING ARTEFACT ARE BOTH REFUTED; ONE TEST REMAINS.**

**Q1 and Q2 are in.** Covered sets: **2000 / 2003 / 2003, three different
digests** — so the sets differ and **(c) is dead.** Stored coverage: **identical
to four decimals**, `counted_tokens` and `excluded_tokens` too — so **the
`NUMERIC(5,4)` rounding artefact I raised against my own query is dead as well.**

**WHAT DECIDES IT IS ONE INTEGER, AND IT IS NOT `by_state`.** A lemma in one
learner's covered set and not another's is `known` for the first and
`learning`/`unknown` for the second. **So if any differing lemma occurs even once
in a transcript, that transcript's coverage MUST differ between those two
learners.** The figures are identical to four decimals. Therefore:

* **differing-lemma occurrences == 0** → **(a).** The coincidence is real and
  forced; `coverage_for` is reading the ledger; **#289 and #88 close as written.**
* **occurrences > 0** → **(b).** Coverage should have differed and did not;
  **#289 reopens** and every coverage figure in this record is one learner's.

**I AM WITHDRAWING THE `by_state` DECISION RULE I PROPOSED LAST TURN, BEFORE THE
RUN RATHER THAN AFTER.** `by_state` *differing* does prove the ledger is read.
But `by_state` *identical* does **not** prove (b) — it is equally what *no
differing lemma occurring at all* looks like, and user 3 has 68 non-covered
extras that could move `by_state` without moving coverage. **A test whose null
result is ambiguous is not the one to hang #289 on.** It is still printed, as
corroboration rather than as the verdict.

**THE OCCURRENCE COUNT GOES THROUGH `compute_coverage` ITSELF** — the differing
lemmas handed in as the entire covered set, so `by_state['known']` is exactly the
number of tokens resolving to one of them. Real tokeniser, real lemmatiser, no
private imports. **Not a substring search:** on a text where the letter-run `the`
appears nine times the lemma resolves once, and that is checked.

**AND THE TEST WAS PROVED ABLE TO FAIL BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN INTO THIS FILE.**
Fired synthetically on both branches — absent → `hits=0`, coverages equal;
present → `hits=2`, coverages diverge — plus a control in which an empty covered
set returns exactly `0.0`. **A diagnostic that cannot separate the two hypotheses
would answer confidently either way**, which is the shape of every defect this
week.

**Q3 — read-only, free, no billed call, and it rolls back explicitly** because
`psycopg_pool`'s context manager commits on a clean exit and nothing here should
ever write.

```bash
set +H; cd /home/bot/english-bot && sudo -u bot .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
"""Q3. Whose coverage is it? READ-ONLY. No billed call. No write.

(c) is refuted: the three covered sets differ. (a) and (b) remain, and they
make INCOMPATIBLE predictions about one number.

THE DECIDING ARGUMENT, DERIVED FROM `compute_coverage` RATHER THAN GUESSED:
a lemma in one learner's COVERED set and not another's is `known` for the
first and either `learning` or `unknown` for the second -- covered for one,
not covered for the other. So IF ANY DIFFERING LEMMA OCCURS EVEN ONCE IN A
TRANSCRIPT, THAT TRANSCRIPT'S COVERAGE MUST DIFFER BETWEEN THOSE TWO
LEARNERS. The stored figures are identical to four decimals. Therefore:

    occurrences == 0  ->  (a). The coincidence is REAL and forced, and
                          `coverage_for` is reading the ledger.
    occurrences  > 0  ->  (b). Coverage should have differed and did not.

Step 3 counts those occurrences THROUGH `compute_coverage` ITSELF, by handing
it the differing lemmas as the entire covered set: `by_state['known']` is then
exactly the number of tokens in the text that resolve to one of them. No
private imports, no re-implementation of the tokenizer, no substring matching
(`'the' in 'theatre'` is why that would be wrong).

Step 4 is the sensitivity control. A comparison that cannot move proves
nothing (#257), so an EMPTY covered set must return 0.0 on every text.
"""
import hashlib
from core.db import connection
from core.lexicon.coverage import compute_coverage
from core.lexicon.states import COVERED_STATES
from core.services.lexicon import ledger, coverage_for
from core.services import video as svc


def md5(lemmas):
    return hashlib.md5(",".join(sorted(lemmas)).encode()).hexdigest()


with connection() as conn:
    rows = svc.selectable(conn)
    users = sorted({r["user_id"] for r in
                    conn.execute("SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM video_coverage")})
    print(f"users: {users}   stored transcripts: {len(rows)}")

    # ---- 1. Does `ledger()` return a DIFFERENT set per user? ---------------
    # This is branch (b) tested at its source, in process, through the real
    # function -- not through SQL, and not by reading the WHERE clause.
    print("\n=== 1. the ledgers, through the real ledger() ===")
    led, cov, vocab = {}, {}, {}
    for u in users:
        led[u] = ledger(conn, u)
        cov[u] = frozenset(l for l, s in led[u].items() if s in COVERED_STATES)
        vocab[u] = frozenset(led[u])
        states = {}
        for s in led[u].values():
            states[s] = states.get(s, 0) + 1
        print(f"  user {u}: rows={len(led[u]):<5} covered={len(cov[u]):<5} "
              f"md5={md5(cov[u])[:16]}  states={dict(sorted(states.items()))}")
    print("  (a python md5 need not equal postgres's -- ORDER BY uses the DB "
          "collation. The SET comparison below is what counts.)")

    union = frozenset().union(*cov.values())
    inter = frozenset.intersection(*cov.values())
    DIFF = union - inter
    print(f"\n  union={len(union)}  intersection={len(inter)}  DIFFERING={len(DIFF)}")
    print(f"  THE DIFFERING LEMMAS: {sorted(DIFF)}")
    for i, a in enumerate(users):
        for b in users[i + 1:]:
            only_a, only_b = sorted(cov[a] - cov[b]), sorted(cov[b] - cov[a])
            print(f"  user {a} vs {b}: only in {a}: {only_a} | only in {b}: {only_b}")
    print(f"\n  LEDGERS ARE USER-SPECIFIC: {len({md5(c) for c in cov.values()}) > 1}"
          "   <- if False, branch (b) is confirmed here and nothing below matters")

    V = frozenset().union(*vocab.values())

    # ---- 2. the real coverage_for, full precision, with the by_state print --
    print("\n=== 2. coverage_for, per learner, per transcript ===")
    print(f"  {'youtube_id':<14} {'user':>5} {'coverage':>14} {'cnt':>5} {'exc':>4}"
          f"  by_state")
    differs = []
    for row in rows:
        vals = set()
        for u in users:
            r = coverage_for(conn, u, row.transcript)
            vals.add(round(r.coverage, 10))
            print(f"  {row.youtube_id:<14} {u:>5} {r.coverage:>14.10f} "
                  f"{r.counted_tokens:>5} {r.excluded_tokens:>4}  "
                  f"{dict(sorted(r.by_state.items()))}")
        if len(vals) > 1:
            differs.append(row.youtube_id)

    # ---- 3. THE DECIDING NUMBER --------------------------------------------
    print("\n=== 3. do the differing lemmas occur at all? (the deciding test) ===")
    diff_ledger = {l: "known" for l in DIFF}
    total_hits = 0
    for row in rows:
        hits = compute_coverage(
            row.transcript, DIFF, ledger=diff_ledger, vocabulary=V
        ).by_state.get("known", 0)
        total_hits += hits
        # Same vocabulary both sides, so `counted` and the lemmatisation are
        # identical and ONLY the covered set varies.
        u_cov = compute_coverage(
            row.transcript, union, ledger={l: "known" for l in union}, vocabulary=V
        ).coverage
        i_cov = compute_coverage(
            row.transcript, inter, ledger={l: "known" for l in inter}, vocabulary=V
        ).coverage
        print(f"  {row.youtube_id:<14} differing-lemma tokens: {hits:>3}   "
              f"coverage(union)={u_cov:.10f}  coverage(intersection)={i_cov:.10f}"
              f"{'   <-- MOVES' if abs(u_cov - i_cov) > 1e-12 else ''}")
    print(f"\n  TOTAL differing-lemma tokens across all transcripts: {total_hits}")

    # ---- 4. sensitivity control --------------------------------------------
    print("\n=== 4. control: can this comparison move at all? ===")
    for row in rows[:2]:
        empty = compute_coverage(
            row.transcript, frozenset(), ledger={}, vocabulary=V
        ).coverage
        full = compute_coverage(
            row.transcript, inter, ledger={l: "known" for l in inter}, vocabulary=V
        ).coverage
        print(f"  {row.youtube_id:<14} covered=<empty> -> {empty:.10f}   "
              f"covered=intersection -> {full:.10f}"
              f"{'   OK' if empty < full else '   <-- CONTROL FAILED'}")

    # ---- verdict ------------------------------------------------------------
    print("\n=== VERDICT ===")
    user_specific = len({md5(c) for c in cov.values()}) > 1
    if not user_specific:
        print("  ledger() returned the SAME covered set for every user -> (b).")
    elif total_hits == 0:
        print("  (a) PROVEN. The ledgers ARE user-specific and NOT ONE of the")
        print(f"  {len(DIFF)} differing lemmas occurs in any of the {len(rows)}")
        print("  transcripts, so identical coverage is FORCED, not suspicious.")
        print("  #289 and #88 close as written.")
    else:
        print(f"  (b) INDICATED. {total_hits} differing-lemma token(s) occur, so")
        print("  coverage SHOULD have differed between learners and did not.")
        print("  #289 reopens. Compare step 2's by_state rows to localise it.")
    print(f"  transcripts where coverage_for differed across learners: {differs}")

    # Nothing above writes. psycopg_pool commits on a clean exit, so this is
    # belt and braces against a later edit adding a write without noticing.
    conn.rollback()
PY
```

**Paste the whole output.** The `=== VERDICT ===` block states which branch, and
the `THE DIFFERING LEMMAS:` line names them — **the bound of six holds only if
user 1's set is a subset of the other two, which the digests cannot say**, so
the list replaces the arithmetic.

#### O. **TWO FREE READS, BOTH SMALL, BOTH RECORDED AS QUESTIONS RATHER THAN FINDINGS.**

**O1 — the six coverage figures are IDENTICAL for all three learners.** *(**ANSWERED IN PART 2026-09-01 AND ESCALATED: the ledgers are 2000 / 2006 / 2071 — three DIFFERENT ledgers — and the coverage is still identical. Superseded by step Q at the head of this list.**)* Coverage
is meant to be a fact about *a learner and a video* — that is why migration 019
gave it a two-key table rather than a column on `videos`. **Identical across three
learners is consistent with three identical ledgers** (all seeded from the
frequency floor, none diverged; **#308** records that every `items` row is
`user_id = 3`). **It is also what a bug that ignores `user_id` would look like.**
One query separates them:

```bash
set +H; sudo -u bot psql -d english_bot -c "SELECT user_id, count(*) AS lexemes, count(*) FILTER (WHERE state IN ('known','mastered')) AS covered FROM user_lexemes GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;"
```

**If the three counts are identical the coverage figures are right and the
learners are genuinely at the same level.** If they differ and the coverage
figures still match, that is a defect and it is bigger than anything in W12b.

**O2 — the CU figure.** `1.7396 CU` unchanged to four decimal places after four
more actor starts needs ≤0.00005 CU — about **0.18 GB-seconds for four actor
starts** — which no actor does. **Read the per-run cost detail on the four new
runs** (console.apify.com → Actor runs → each run → cost). The `$0.58` total
being unchanged is fine and expected; it is the CU digit that wants a second
look. **#321 is why this is not being taken at face value.**

#### K. **#289 — THE BAND RE-VALIDATION. FREE, READ-ONLY, AND IT IS THE LAST THING BETWEEN PHASE B AND A VERDICT.**

**WHY THIS CANNOT BE RUN OFF THE FIXTURES AND MUST RUN ON THE HOST — the reason
is structural, not convenience.** `coverage_for` (`services/lexicon.py`) computes
coverage from **`ledger(conn, user_id)`** — the learner's own known-lexeme set.
**Coverage is a fact about a learner AND a video**, which is why migration 019
gave it a two-key table instead of a column. There is no learner ledger in this
repository and there cannot be one; the transcripts are on the host and so are
the ledgers. **Nothing was run locally and nothing could have been.**

**AND THE NUMBERS ALREADY EXIST.** `_recompute_coverage` ran inside both H
invocations, so `video_coverage` holds a current row per learner per video,
stamped with the `lexicon_digest` that produced it. **This is a SELECT, not a
recomputation** — it reports what the pipeline actually computed rather than what
a second implementation would compute, which is CLAUDE.md §3 rule 5's shape.

**K1 — the per-video table. `LEFT JOIN` deliberately: a stored transcript with no
coverage row must appear as a null rather than vanish from the report.**

```bash
set +H; sudo -u bot psql -d english_bot -c "SELECT v.id, v.youtube_id, v.channel_id, v.captions_kind, v.transcript_lang, v.duration_s, length(v.transcript) AS chars, c.user_id, round(c.coverage*100, 1) AS cov_pct, c.proper_nouns_detected AS proper_nouns, c.casing, (c.coverage >= 0.93 AND c.coverage <= 0.98) AS in_band FROM videos v LEFT JOIN video_coverage c ON c.video_id = v.id WHERE v.transcript_status = 'ok' ORDER BY v.id, c.user_id;"
```

**K2 — the distribution, per learner. This is the number #289 asks for.**

```bash
set +H; sudo -u bot psql -d english_bot -c "SELECT c.user_id, count(*) AS videos, count(*) FILTER (WHERE c.coverage >= 0.93 AND c.coverage <= 0.98) AS in_band, count(*) FILTER (WHERE c.coverage < 0.93) AS below_band, count(*) FILTER (WHERE c.coverage > 0.98) AS above_band, count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT c.proper_nouns_detected) AS degraded_288, round(min(c.coverage)*100,1) AS min_pct, round(max(c.coverage)*100,1) AS max_pct FROM video_coverage c JOIN videos v ON v.id = c.video_id WHERE v.transcript_status = 'ok' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;"
```

**K3 — the real gate, exercised rather than described.** `assign` applies the
band as an ADMISSION gate and #288's degraded exclusion, and prints both counts
plus the ranking. **Dry by default; it makes no external call and writes
nothing.** Take `--user` from K2's `user_id` column.

```bash
set +H; cd /home/bot/english-bot && sudo -u bot .venv/bin/python -m core.video.assign --user 3 --week-of 2026-09-01
```

**Paste all three.** A count this file predicts is not verification of it.

#### L. **WHAT THE ANSWER WILL PROBABLY BE, DERIVED FROM WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN — WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE THE NUMBERS SO IT CANNOT BE FITTED TO THEM.**

**THE BAND MAY NOT EVEN BE THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, AND THAT WOULD ITSELF BE
#289's FINDING.** Two exclusions sit upstream of it, and both are computable from
the committed listing without any coverage figure at all:

| video | channel | duration | kind | `length_fit` | upstream status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `QyRqlTV60zM` | TED-Ed | 5.7 min | **manual** | **1.00** | admissible |
| `9sSD2IFGSLw` | English with Lucy | 13.8 min | **manual** | 0.90 | admissible |
| `y_525lzqbg0` | Friends | 3.5 min | generated | 0.89 | **#288 exclusion likely** |
| `ScmC5E7titM` | English with Lucy | 0.9 min | generated | 0.22 | **#288 exclusion likely** |
| `5E5tNu4NsxM` | Friends | **0.3 min** | generated | **0.07** | **#288 exclusion likely** |
| `l29K-ZkARmE` | — | — | — | — | not in the committed listing |

**(1) #288.** Auto-generated YouTube captions are lowercase, so
`proper_nouns_detected` comes back false and `assign` excludes the row **whatever
its coverage is** — the number is inflated and the exclusion is the point.
**Three of the six are auto-generated by the listing.** K1's
`proper_nouns` column settles it per row rather than by assumption.

**(2) LENGTH IS SCORED AND NOT GATED, AND ONE ROW MAKES THAT UNCOMFORTABLE.**
`5E5tNu4NsxM` is **17 seconds** with a transcript reported at **234
characters**. `length_fit` gives it 0.07 and nothing excludes it. **A coverage
percentage over 234 characters is not a measurement of a learner's coverage; it
is a measurement of one short paragraph** — and it will land wherever those few
tokens happen to fall, including inside 93–98% by accident. **That is a
different defect from the band being wrong, and if it shows up in K1 it should
be filed rather than absorbed into #289.**

**SO THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION — *three videos assigned, each between 93% and
98%* — HAS AT MOST THREE ADMISSIBLE CANDIDATES BEFORE THE BAND IS APPLIED**, and
possibly two. **If fewer than three survive, the slice cannot meet its criterion
on this pool for a reason that is upstream of the band**, and the honest report
is *the pool is too thin*, not *the band is too narrow*.

**THE RULE, RESTATED SO IT IS NOT RE-ARGUED WHEN THE NUMBERS ARRIVE.** #289's
own wording: **if almost none land inside, that is the finding and the slice
stops.** CLAUDE.md §3 rule 7: **the acceptance bar is never quietly lowered.**
Not by widening 93–98%, not by passing `--allow-degraded`, not by ranking around
the gate, not by assigning the best available. **`assign` already refuses rather
than filling a week** — that refusal is the correct outcome, not a bug to route
around.

**IF THE BAND HOLDS — three or more inside 93–98%, on non-degraded rows —
then #88 closes on the validated number.** #88 records that the three source
documents disagree: **PRD §2.1 says 95–98%, PRD §7.2's formula says 0.95–0.98,
`docs/TASKS-v3-web.md` says 93–98%**, and W12 was to pick one and say so.
**Picking is not enough and never was: whichever is picked has to be the one the
measurement supports.** Close #88 by making all four sites agree with what K1
and K2 show, and record the distribution beside it as the evidence.

**WHAT PHASE B WOULD STILL OWE BEFORE W13, IF THE BAND HOLDS:**

1. **The FETCH fixtures, committed.** `run2/actor.fetch.001..003.json` are the
   first fetch responses this repository could hold; every recorded response so
   far is a listing. **And #317's outstanding half with them** — the full
   14,374-byte `actor.list.001.json` is still only on the host, so the committed
   fixture remains a re-serialised slice without the byte-identity #317 was
   ruled in to guarantee.
2. **#326 and #327**, both filed today, both in the money path.
3. **#316** — three accents still authored rather than watched. Three minutes.
4. **#319(b)** — a run or dataset id in the dumped body, unchecked on `run2`.
5. **#290 / #320** — the FLOOR still has no model. #321's ruling stands: it does
   not need a correction, it needs a different model, and the second run is the

**WHAT CHANGED, IN ONE PARAGRAPH.** The four `NoTranscriptFound` failures of the
first billed run were **not an IP block**. The pipeline sent
`transcript_type: "manual"` and never set `languages`, so the actor's `["en"]`
default applied and the question was *a manual track whose language code is
exactly `en`* — which four of the five videos do not have. **Confirmed on
production before anything was rewritten:** the same video (`9sSD2IFGSLw`), the
same actor, the same IP, the same minute, with `transcript_type: "any"` returned
**HTTP 201, `success True`, `error_message None`, `retry_attempts None`, 10,373
characters.** One parameter.

**SO THESE ARE WITHDRAWN, NAMED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED:** the residential
proxy (Option A) was never the lever; *accept ~20% and list 5x* (Option C)
answered a supply problem that does not exist; and the *20% fetch rate* is not a
fetch rate at all — it is four correct refusals of a malformed query. **The
re-cost stands: ~$0.03 per video, so 72 videos is ~$2 and not $41.76.** 6f's
free question — *what does the `Actors` line actually price* — **is answered and
kept**: it is compute, and the compute went into forty internal retries of
queries that could never succeed.

**WHAT IS COMMITTED AND NOT DEPLOYED.** The per-video query, `languages` from
the track list, `include_metadata: false` on both actor calls, and the terminal
verdict narrowed to *the free listing enumerated the tracks and found none*.
**No migration. `schema_version` stays at 20** — `failed` is already in 019's
CHECK, so the second `unavailable` producer was deleted without a schema change.

**WHY THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT TIDINESS.** Until D is deployed,
`record_transcript_failure` still promotes an exhausted retryable failure to
`unavailable`, and `fetch_transcripts` still returns a terminal verdict for an
empty response. **Reset the rows before the code and the next run walks them
straight back through both doors** — the second one silently, after three
failures, looking exactly like the pool simply not having those videos.

**Read first. This prints what is about to change and changes nothing.**

```bash
set +H; sudo -u bot psql -d english_bot -c "SELECT id, youtube_id, transcript_status, transcript_attempts, left(coalesce(transcript_last_error,''), 60) AS err FROM videos ORDER BY id;"
```

**Expect exactly the six rows recorded on 2026-09-01:** `3 QyRqlTV60zM ok 0`,
`4 l29K-ZkARmE pending 0`, and **ids 1, 2, 5, 6 `unavailable 1`** with *"actor
returned a row with no transcript text"*. **If any row differs — a different
status, a different attempt count, a seventh row — STOP and paste it.** The
`WHERE` below is written against that exact state.

**Then the write. The database is named, the rows are named by id AND by the
status they must currently hold, and the count is returned.**

```bash
set +H; sudo -u bot psql -d english_bot -c "UPDATE videos SET transcript_status = 'pending', transcript_attempts = 0, transcript_last_error = NULL WHERE id IN (1, 2, 5, 6) AND transcript_status = 'unavailable' RETURNING id, youtube_id, transcript_status, transcript_attempts;"
```

**`AND transcript_status = 'unavailable'` is a guard, not decoration:** if the
rows are not in the state the read showed, the `UPDATE` matches nothing and says
so, instead of overwriting whatever they had become. **It must return exactly
four rows.** Anything else — three, five, zero — is a state this instruction was
not written for; stop and paste it.

**`transcript_last_error = NULL` is deliberate and is a change of meaning.** The
old text asserts *"actor returned a row with no transcript text"*, which is true
of the old query and would now be read as a fact about the video. **The reason
those four failed is recorded here, in #322 and #324, not in a column a future
run will re-read.**

After H, coverage exists for real transcripts for the first time. **What Phase B
owes is the distribution: coverage for both learners over every stored
transcript, and how many land inside 93–98%.**

Not by widening the band, not by ranking around it, not by assigning the best
available. **Report the number and the reason.** Resolve **#88** — the three
source documents say 95–98%, 0.95–0.98 and 93–98% — **in the same pass, on the
measurement rather than by picking one.**

— **the URL ends at `run-sync-get-dataset-items`, with no `?` and no `token=`.**

**(2) THE CAPTION-KIND CHECK, FIRING BEFORE PAYMENT.** **GOOD:** a block reading

never folded into `generated`**, because an absent field and an auto-generated
track are different facts (#257). It must appear **above** `transcripts to
fetch`. **ALSO GOOD:** `caption kinds: CHECK FAILED (…)` followed by the run
continuing to `Fetching N transcript(s)` — the check is advisory and **must not
abort a paid run**. **BAD:** the block appearing after the fetch, or the run
stopping on a failed check.

console.apify.com → **Actor runs** → the run for
`johnvc/YoutubeTranscripts` at this timestamp → its **cost** field; and
**Billing → Usage** for the same period, which is where compute units, storage
and proxy show up. **GOOD is any real number, because the multiplier is the
output.** Record `console_charge ÷ $0.000118`. **That multiplier is what turns
the FLOOR into a usable estimate for the 21-unit run, and it is the reason #319
and #320 are not being fixed before this run** — an estimator tuned against a
bill nobody has seen is precision on the wrong digit.
